extracted.intended_audience: machine learning engineers, dataset creators, and HCI/CSCW researchers interested in dataset documentation and ML ethics
extracted.subtask_description: Assessing and producing dataset context documents (Datasheets and similar) to surface ethical, legal, provenance, and quality information so ML engineers can recognize, particularize, and judge ethical issues in training data.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ethical sensitivity — Recognition
rubrics_metrics.description: Recognition is the moment of noticing: a shift from seeing the task as primarily technical to ethical, where a worker perceives information that signals the situation requires ethical judgment.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Context documents (e.g., Datasheets) may act as cues that trigger recognition. Recognition can be observed during task execution (think-aloud) and may be prompted by explicit questions or data characteristics. The paper counts recognition only when participants outwardly expressed concern; cues include text snippets, provenance info, and dataset characteristics.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ethical sensitivity — Particularization
rubrics_metrics.description: Particularization is any kind of understanding-building activity: seeking information, reflecting, and making developmental evaluations about the situation, stakeholders, consequences, and responsibilities.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Particularization includes reflecting on beliefs, seeking information, and referring to external standards (policies, codes). Datasheets are intended to support particularization by providing concrete dataset characteristics, prompting reasoning about likely effects, and helping stakeholders identify what questions to ask and evaluate suitability, risks, failure cases, and mitigation strategies.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ethical sensitivity — Judgment
rubrics_metrics.description: Judgment involves formulating the morally ideal course of action, deciding what one intends to do, and executing/implementing that intention.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: In ML development judgment could lead to implementing mitigation (e.g., bias mitigation, encryption), refusing to build, or proceeding without adjustments. Recognition and particularization feed into judgment with feed-forward and feedback interactions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Include context of development and data collection
rubrics_metrics.description: Context documents should describe the context of development and how the data were collected (provenance).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provenance aids understanding of biases and legal/consent issues. The paper highlights that Datasheets and related context documents explicitly ask for development context and collection procedures to allow users to reason about dataset fitness and ethical implications.

rubrics_metrics.name: Report measures of data distribution
rubrics_metrics.description: Datasheets should include measures/statistics of the dataset distribution (e.g., demographic breakdowns, frequencies of attributes).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explicit percentages or counts (e.g., percent male/female, percent white/non-white, counts of occlusion, glasses, multiple faces) help users detect imbalance and anticipate model performance disparities. These characteristics can prompt recognition of fairness/privacy issues and support particularization.

rubrics_metrics.name: Report model performance and suitability metrics
rubrics_metrics.description: Context documents should include measures of model performance or guidance about expected performance when relevant to the dataset.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Performance metrics enable evaluation of dataset suitability for given tasks and comparison across subgroups; model cards and related documents complement datasheets by reporting such model-level metrics.

rubrics_metrics.name: Document ethical and legal concerns explicitly
rubrics_metrics.description: Context documents should include explicit ethical and legal questions and disclosures (e.g., whether ethical review was conducted).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples of explicit questions: “Were any ethical review processes conducted?” Directly asking about ethics can surface issues; some documents also rely on reporting characteristics (rather than direct ethics questions) to prompt reflection.

rubrics_metrics.name: State intended uses and prohibited uses
rubrics_metrics.description: Datasheets should state tasks for which the dataset is intended or should not be used.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Question examples: “Are there any tasks for which the dataset should not be used?” Specifying appropriate and inappropriate uses helps prevent misuse (e.g., surveillance, policing) and supports ethical decision-making.

rubrics_metrics.name: Warn about uses that could result in unfair treatment
rubrics_metrics.description: Context documents should surface anything future users might need to know to avoid uses that could result in unfair treatment of individuals or groups.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Directly prompting authors to reflect on potential unfair outcomes encourages disclosure of limitations, edge cases, and societal impacts; such warnings support both recognition and particularization.

rubrics_metrics.name: Disclose consent, licensing, and subject awareness
rubrics_metrics.description: Datasheets should document whether subjects of data consented, the licenses under which data were collected, and whether subjects were aware of collections/uses.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The paper's example notes scraped images posted under permissive Creative Commons but acknowledges that subjects in photos may not have consented—this distinction matters for privacy and legality. Documentation should clarify these provenance and consent details.

rubrics_metrics.name: Surface demographic oversampling and sampling biases
rubrics_metrics.description: Datasheets should disclose deliberate or incidental sampling strategies that produce demographic imbalances (e.g., oversampling of particular gender/race groups).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Making such imbalances explicit (e.g., '71% men, 89% white') allows engineers to anticipate fairness problems and consider mitigations, such as re-sampling, targeted data collection, or adjusted evaluation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Discuss tradeoffs between collecting sensitive attributes and fairness
rubrics_metrics.description: Documentation should acknowledge that collecting sensitive attributes (race, gender) may be necessary to detect or mitigate bias but increases privacy risks.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Datasheets should present this tension and possible mitigation strategies (encryption of sensitive attributes, access controls, differential privacy) so practitioners can make informed choices.

rubrics_metrics.name: Include potential failure cases, societal implications, and risks
rubrics_metrics.description: Context documents should help builders consider societal implications, risks, and failure cases of dataset-driven systems.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explicit sections encouraging authors to list failure modes, downstream harms (e.g., 'suspicious behavior' detection as pre-crime), and contexts where the dataset is inappropriate improve particularization and ethical judgment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Be legible to non-expert stakeholders (lay language)
rubrics_metrics.description: Datasheets should be written in language accessible to managers, users, citizens, and auditors, not only technical audiences.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Legibility to non-experts empowers oversight and accountability; the paper emphasizes Datasheets' lay-language design to broaden stakeholder engagement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Tailor scope and specificity to audience and purpose
rubrics_metrics.description: Choose document scope: technique- or domain-specific versus general-purpose, and match depth/format to audience (technical report vs lay summary).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Technique-specific docs (e.g., NLP data statements) can be more precise; other formats include technical reports, lay-language documents, and programmatic templates—selecting appropriate scope improves usefulness and uptake.

rubrics_metrics.name: Encourage dataset authors' reflective documentation
rubrics_metrics.description: Datasheets should encourage creators to reflect critically about dataset strengths, weaknesses, collection choices, and ethical considerations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The goal is to 'encourage creative, critical thought' by authors; prompts and explicit questions can help authors articulate limitations and reasoning, aiding downstream users.

rubrics_metrics.name: Disclose limits to transparency and interpretability
rubrics_metrics.description: Documentation should note limits to transparency due to model interpretability, IP, privacy laws, organizational secrecy, or unavailable provenance.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Acknowledging transparency constraints helps users understand what cannot be known and suggests where oversight or additional investigation is needed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Context documents as cues to check for issues during development
rubrics_metrics.description: Design documentation to function as a practical cue that prompts builders to 'check for issues at the time of model development.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Framing datasheets/nutrition labels/model cards as checklists or prompts can integrate ethical review into normal development workflows and increase timely recognition of problems.

rubrics_metrics.name: Empirical usage metrics for Datasheets
rubrics_metrics.description: When evaluating a context document intervention, measure whether participants opened and referred to the Datasheet and how often they mentioned ethical issues during task performance.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The study measured opening/usage times, frequency/timing of ethical mentions in think-aloud, and whether particularization occurred with the Datasheet on-screen; these are concrete proxies for impact on recognition and particularization.

rubrics_metrics.name: Design documentation to enable evaluation of dataset appropriateness for purposes
rubrics_metrics.description: Datasheets should provide enough contextual and statistical information for readers to evaluate whether the dataset is appropriate for their intended task and deployment context.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This includes documenting collection context, distributions, known limitations, intended uses, and potential harms so readers can judge suitability and plan mitigations if necessary.
